ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper part is the inductor L, and the right side is the resistor R; the two are connected into a single-loop series branch; the left port is labeled with voltage u, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative; the current arrow i points to the right on the upper branch, indicating that the current flows through the series-connected L and R. Reasoning: This circuit can be regarded as a series RL branch applied across the two terminals of voltage u. Given i = 5 sin(ωt) A, therefore the maximum value of the current is 5 A, and the effective value I = 5/√2 A. The resistance R = 2 Ω, and the inductive reactance X_L = ωL = 2 Ω. The magnitude of the series impedance |Z| = √(R^2 + X_L^2) = √(2^2 + 2^2) = 2√2 Ω. The effective value of the voltage U = I|Z| = (5/√2)(2√2) = 10 V.
